relevance_note: A WES cohort of 37 MMS patients in which one person carries a homozygous GAMT variant: "GAMT (patient 16)" with "NM_138924.3: c.327G>A" (Homozygous).
method_note: Built with a short script from my reading; spans are substrings of the Table 1 row for patient 16 (patients as rows; label column 'Patient' holds bare numbers, but the text uses 'patient 16', so rule 1 gives that label). Only patient 16 has a GAMT variant; the other 15 diagnosed patients (other genes) and 21 undiagnosed patients are out of scope (cohort_size_as_stated = 37 patients; 100 individuals sequenced including relatives). Parents of patient 16 are mentioned only collectively ('within different trios with apparently unrelated parents'; 'segregation from apparently unaffected carrier parents') with no individual-level detail, so they get no rows. Inheritance left 'not reported': the variant is homozygous and the group statement says the parents are carriers (biparental), which has no enum value; the statement is quoted in parental_testing_statement. Variant type: the table cell reads 'Splice donor defect/Synonymous'; recorded as 'splice' (Table 2 also counts 'Splice defect'). 'Age at WES' 44 recorded as age at last evaluation (no unit printed; years assumed for ISO from the cohort age description). Ethnicity left not reported: the Results say only 'the vast majority' of the cohort is Greek-Cypriot. Consanguinity 'no' from 'apparently unrelated parents'. 'hand biting' recorded as a feature but the checklist item 'self-injurious behaviour' left not reported (not stated as self-injury). 'epileptic encephalopathy' marks seizures observed; abnormal EEG not stated. Contradictions noted in the paper (not about patient 16): the text says '15 genes' but lists 14; S2 Fig legend says HECW2 variants in 'patient 13' while the text says patient 12; 'Arg1575Glu' vs 'Arg1575Gln'.

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: Family-based (trio) whole-exome sequencing, with candidate variants confirmed by Sanger sequencing
span: AGTPBP1 (patient 15) and GAMT (patient 16), as mentioned above, within different trios with apparently unrelated parents
Family-based WES and subsequent analysis performed on 32 families revealed 17 potentially pathogenic SNVs or small indels in 16 MMS patients

Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) amplification and subsequent bi-directional Sanger sequencing using the ABI 3130xl Genetic Analyzer (Applied Biosystems, Foster City, CA, USA) were used to confirm these variants.
